subject: Crediting approach for residency + HSM: invoice timing and SOW split
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@pioneerhealth.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Cameron Lee <cameron.lee@pioneerhealth.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Residency + HSM pricing: clarification and how credits will show on invoices

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Pioneer is aligned to move forward with Redwood for the inference platform, but procurement needs a bit more color on how the compliance add-ons will be billed and credited. A few asks from our side: 

- We want audit log retention for 5 years (US data residency). Please confirm the monthly recurring cost and whether that can be credited if we front-load implementation fees.
- HSM: we expect 2 dedicated HSM seats for the production tenant + a staging seat. Your product team described both a one-time provisioning fee and a recurring seat fee — can you show the two options side-by-side?
- Residency transition credits: we have a three-phase plan (pilot -> staged -> go-live). Procurement would like to know whether credits for residency/HSM are amortized monthly across the contract or applied as an upfront credit on the implementation invoice.
- We also need a clean SOW line-itemization for legal (implementation hours, data migration, and a separate recurring compliance SKU).

I've attached our draft SOW (internal). Can you respond with (1) two canonical billing options (amortized vs upfront credit) with example invoice lines, and (2) any concessions available if we commit 24 months instead of 12?

Appreciate a short write-up we can share with our finance/legal teams.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Senior Procurement Manager
Pioneer Health

Attachment: Pioneer_SOW_draft_v1.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@pioneerhealth.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 13:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Residency + HSM pricing: clarification and how credits will show on invoices

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Below are two practical approaches we use frequently for customers like Pioneer. I included example invoice lines and a short recommendation. I've attached our pricing sheet for reference.

Option A — Amortized credit (recommended for predictable unit economics)
- Implementation SOW (one-time): Implementation services — $120,000 (one-time)
- Compliance add-ons (recurring): Audit logs (5y) — $3,200/month; HSM seat (prod) — $1,800/seat/month; Staging HSM — $900/month
- Crediting: Redwood applies a monthly amortized credit equal to the agreed implementation concession (e.g., $60,000) over the first 12 months: Invoice example: 
  - Month 1: Recurring charges $X — Implementation invoice $120,000 — Applied credit $5,000 (amortized)
  - Month 2–12: Recurring charges — Applied credit $5,000/month
Pros: smooth revenue recognition for Pioneer, predictable monthly net cash flow.
Cons: bookkeeping required to track carry-forward credits.

Option B — Upfront credit against implementation invoice (preferred by legal for clear one-off settlement)
- Implementation SOW (one-time): Implementation services — $120,000
- Redwood issues an upfront concession as a credit memo applied immediately to the implementation invoice (e.g., $60,000), leaving Pioneer to pay a net $60,000 on the implementation invoice. Recurring charges billed normally thereafter.
Pros: simpler for Pioneer accounting (single settled invoice).
Cons: Redwood recognizes less contracted ARR in year 1; less granular amortization.

Concessions for 24-month commit: we can offer a 20% discount on audit log recurring charges and waive the staging HSM monthly fee for the first 3 months. Alternatively, if Pioneer prefers amortization, we can extend the amortization window to 18 months to lower monthly net charges.

Recommendation: go with Option A (amortized) for predictability, but if legal needs a single settled invoice we can convert to Option B. Either way we will provide example invoice lines and an updated SOW with split line-items (implementation, migration, compliance recurring) — attaching the draft pricing sheet now.

Next step: I can join a quick procurement call later this week (Wed/Thu). Does 11am ET Thu work?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Compliance_Pricing_Sheet_20260914.xlsx

- Legal will want explicit language in the SOW about credit carry-forward and how it impacts termination/true-up. Can you ask legal if we should cap outstanding credits on termination? My preference is to cap at remaining unpaid recurring charges; let me know if that is acceptable to finance.
- For HSM, let's present both a one-time provisioning license (OPEX->CAPEX ask) and a recurring managed HSM fee; create two SKU lines so Pioneer can choose.
- Also: can we include a sample invoice PDF showing the credit as a negative line item? Procurement often wants to see exactly how this posts. We have an example in our playbook (see Invoice_Line_Examples.pdf attached).

Ben — can you draft two sample invoice PDFs (Option A amortized across 12 months & Option B upfront credit) and upload the DocuSign-ready SOW once Jonas confirms wording?

Laura Bennett
